prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Emoji · 服务状态 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "服务" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 96px
  col 2: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 21px · one-line width 61px
  col 3: header "可用率" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 61px
  col 4: header "最近事件" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 437px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 480px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"An at-a-glance operations dashboard for comparing service health, availability, and recent incidents across five services.","reading":"Readers anchor on the service name in column 1, quickly scan the status icon/word in column 2 and the uptime percentage in column 3, then read column 4 only when they need incident context. Rows should read as service units, while columns 2 and 3 form the fast comparison pair.","groups":["Columns 2 状态 and 3 可用率 belong together as the health metrics: categorical status plus quantitative uptime.","Column 1 服务 is the row identity and anchor for every comparison.","Column 4 最近事件 is supporting narrative, read after status and uptime."],"keep_intact":["Service names: API Gateway, 支付服务, 消息推送, 对象存储, CDN","Status labels and icons: 正常, 降级, 故障","Availability percentages: 99.99%, 99.12%, 99.97%, 97.40%","Timestamps such as 03:12 and identifiers such as 华东 2"],"may_wrap":["Column 4 event descriptions; they are long narrative text and can wrap naturally.","Headers only if unavoidable; service names, status labels, and percentages should not wrap."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[126,84,88,181],"idea":"Balanced scan: give each column a comfortable minimum while reserving the largest share for event text, so all four fields read evenly."},{"name":"B","widths":[118,82,82,197],"idea":"Event-led: pin service, status, and uptime to their one-line minimums and spend the remaining width on 最近事件, accepting two- to three-line event cells."},{"name":"C","widths":[120,96,96,167],"idea":"Status-metric emphasis: widen 状态 and 可用率 beyond their minimums for fast icon and percentage scanning, while keeping service names intact and letting event text wrap more."}]}
